name: Saint Blaise
history: A bishop of Sebaste in Armenia, now Sivas in Turkey, martyred in the early fourth century. Tradition says that on the way to his death he saved a boy who was choking on a fish bone, and so on his feast the Church blesses throats with two crossed candles. He is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers, the saints popularly invoked in particular needs.
life: Almost all we know of Blaise comes from his legend, written centuries later, though his cult is ancient in both East and West. The story tells of a physician who became bishop of Sebaste and, when persecution came under the emperor Licinius, withdrew to a cave in the hills, where wild animals came to him to be healed. Hunters found him and he was taken to the governor. On the way a mother brought her son, choking on a fish bone, and Blaise prayed over him and he recovered. A poor woman whose pig had been carried off by a wolf had it returned at his word, and she later brought candles to his prison. He was torn with iron combs, like those used to card wool, and beheaded. Wool combers took him as their patron, and in the wool towns of Yorkshire his day was once kept with processions. The blessing of throats keeps his memory alive in parishes everywhere.
prayerTo: Saint Blaise, bishop and martyr, you cared for the sick and brought healing even on the road to your death. Pray for all who are ill, especially those with diseases of the throat. Guard my speech, that it may give praise to God and do no harm to others, and pray that I may be delivered from every evil of body and soul. Amen.
penance: Receive the blessing of throats if your parish offers it. Guard your tongue today: speak no word of complaint or gossip.
meditation: Yesterday’s candles are often used for today’s blessing. Ask God to bless not only your throat but every word that passes through it.
